transfer.stem: Which plan keeps the payment rules and the budget correct?
transfer.passage:
Planning a small shopping trip
We bought only things we could carry home. A shop planned to sell locally made baskets, but we had no report that they had all been sold. At one counter, card payment was available. This did not tell us whether cash was accepted there or what other counters accepted. A different stall accepted cash but not cards.
We asked how much a repair would cost; no price was supplied. I usually spent less money when I took a shopping list. Less did not mean that I spent nothing. Before shopping, we also practised keeping money for the bus home.
In that separate budget exercise, we had 12 yuan and the stated bus fare was 3 yuan. We moved exactly 3 yuan into the bus-fare tray, leaving 9 yuan available for other plans. The amounts belonged to the exercise, not to the original instruction to keep a little money. The picture showed fictional cash and a card without denominations.
Finally, a coin rolled beneath the ticket machine. This told us where it went, not that it had been put into the machine or picked up again.

options.text: The counter forbade cash; the stall accepted cash but not cards; the exercise left 9 yuan after reserving 3 yuan.
The counter allowed card payment; the stall accepted both cash and cards; the exercise left 9 yuan after reserving 3 yuan.
The counter allowed card payment; the stall accepted cash but not cards; the exercise left 9 yuan after reserving 3 yuan.
The counter allowed card payment; the stall accepted cash but not cards; the exercise left all 12 yuan to spend after reserving 3 yuan.

answer.display: The counter allowed card payment; the stall accepted cash but not cards; the exercise left 9 yuan after reserving 3 yuan.
